claim: Erdman testified that after the ODNI Director's Initiatives Group circulated investigative journalist Steve Baker's information about the January 6 pipe-bomb suspect, the CIA monitored DIG members' computers and communications, opened investigations summoning them to a polygraph facility, fired a contractor-whistleblower one day after he reported to the DIG, and — after the DIG was dissolved in January 2026 — clawed back 40 boxes of JFK assassination files and MKULTRA records that had been queued for declassification.

sources.label: Written Testimony of James E. Erdman III, U.S. Senate HSGAC, May 13, 2026 — 'DIG investigations were being undermined from within the IC' section
sources.quote: Sometime shortly after, the CIA began monitoring the computer usage of the DIG officers involved in handling Steve Baker's information and pulling their electronic communications. The CIA also opened investigations into these individuals and began contacting them demanding that they report to a separate facility to be interviewed as part of this investigation. That facility is known as a location where polygraph interviews are conducted. ... After the DIG shutdown ... the CIA took back 40 boxes of documents being processed for declassification. They were JFK assassination files, and they have not yet been released. They also took back MKULTRA files the DNI was going to process for possible declassification.

notes: Group B (sworn allegation) from capture DYYLACQDnG1 — the surveillance-of-oversight thread from Erdman's testimony, promoted from notes to its own card per the prior proposed-push. Verbatim. Erdman frames these as illegal monitoring of an oversight body (DIG, the ODNI Director's Initiatives Group created by DNI Gabbard April 2025). The Steve Baker thread: Baker reported he had assessed that a current CIA employee, then a Capitol Police officer, planted the Jan 5 2026... [Jan 5 2021] pipe bombs at the DNC/RNC; the DIG did not corroborate it but circulated his information; PDDNI Aaron Lukas passed it to CIA Deputy Director Michael Ellis, after which it spread across the administration — Erdman ties this to the DIG's December 2025 pause and January 2026 dissolution. These are attributed allegations under oath; the CIA disputes the DIG's characterizations and (per the testimony) refused to provide records. Companion to 2026-covid-origins-001/-002/-003.
